title: Transport cohomology through bijective restrictions in a commuting square
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $g:X'\to X$, $i:X_0\to X$, $j:X'_0\to X'$, $k:X'_0\to X_0$ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] with $g\circ j=i\circ k$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and $q\geq0$. Suppose the canonical restrictions $i^*:H^q(X,F_{ab})\to H^q(X_0,i^{-1}F_{ab})$ and $j^*:H^q(X',(g^{-1}F)_{ab})\to H^q(X'_0,j^{-1}(g^{-1}F)_{ab})$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] are bijective. Then there exist additive equivalences $b_1:H^q(X,F_{ab})\simeq H^q(X_0,(i^{-1}F)_{ab})$ and $b_2:H^q(X',g^{-1}F_{ab})\simeq H^q(X'_0,k^{-1}(i^{-1}F)_{ab})$ with $b_2(g^*x)=k^*(b_1(x))$ for every $x$.

proof.text: Obtain c1,c2,c3 and their commuting-square equation from the module coefficient compatibility theorem.

Use AddEquiv.ofBijective on the two assumed restrictions to define r1,r2. Set b1=r1 followed by c1, and b2=c2 followed by r2 followed by c3. AddEquiv.trans preserves invertibility. By definition these equivalences act by exactly the maps in the compatibility equation, so that equation proves the result.
